memory_update.text: TENB should remain in the Layer 1 cloud-security control-plane universe as an underfollowed mid-cap exposure-management/CNAPP candidate; key verification fields are Tenable One growth, cloud module adoption, CIEM/DSPM/AI-SPM evidence, and enterprise net retention.

RPD should remain as a speculative small-cap CNAPP/compliance-automation candidate; survival depends on evidence that InsightCloudSec is strategically important and not overwhelmed by larger platform competitors.

PD should remain as an underfollowed operations-automation control-plane candidate; survival depends on measurable AIOps and automation attach rates, enterprise expansion, and proof that AI/cloud complexity creates incremental demand rather than merely rebranding incident management.

PANW is now the key reference anchor for machine/AI identity security after completing the CyberArk acquisition on February 11, 2026; do not treat CYBR as an independent US-listed candidate in future layers unless only used as historical context.

QUALYS was identified as a plausible additional mid-cap cloud-security/compliance candidate but excluded due to the four-candidate cap; evaluate in a later pass alongside Elastic, Dynatrace, Zscaler, SentinelOne, Jamf, OneSpan, and federal/compliance niche names such as Telos.

node: Cloud security, identity, observability, and automation control-plane software
summary: Expanded the node with a two-lane universe: one mega-cap reference anchor that now owns the most obvious machine-identity reference asset, plus three smaller US-listed underfollowed candidates tied to cloud exposure management, CNAPP/compliance automation, and incident/AIOps remediation. The strongest underfollowed matches for this pass are TENB, RPD, and PD because their products sit in control-plane workflows that become more necessary as cloud estates, identities, alerts, and compliance scope expand. This is research support only, not a trading recommendation.
